title: High-dimensional coherence to entanglement transduction under canonical noise
authors: Asad Ali, Aiham M. Rostom, Saif Al-Kuwari, H. Kuniyil, M. T. Rahim, Saeed Haddadi
abstract: We develop an analytical framework for coherence-to-entanglement conversion in bipartite high-dimensional quantum systems, so-called qunits. An arbitrary coherent input qunit is coupled to an incoherent ancilla through a generalized controlled-shift operation, producing a maximally correlated bipartite state. By analyzing the partial transpose of the output state, we establish an exact dimension-independent connection between the input coherence and the generated entanglement. We then study how this conversion is affected by three standard noise processes applied after the conversion step: phase damping, global depolarizing noise, and independent amplitude damping. The resulting expressions show that these channels degrade entanglement in qualitatively different ways. Phase damping leads to a uniform attenuation of the entanglement generated from coherence, depolarizing noise introduces pairwise thresholds associated with entanglement sudden death, and amplitude damping produces an asymmetric decay governed by relaxation toward the ground state. For maximally coherent inputs, the general results reduce to simple closed-form behavior, allowing direct comparison of the three noise mechanisms as the system dimension increases. In particular, global depolarizing noise exhibits a dimension-dependent sudden-death threshold, while amplitude damping leads to a smooth suppression in the maximally coherent case. These results provide useful analytical benchmarks for high-dimensional resource conversion and for assessing noisy entanglement generation in qudit-based quantum-information settings.
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework to quantify the conversion of coherence into entanglement in high-dimensional qudit systems. It rigorously analyzes how this generated entanglement degrades when subjected to phase damping, global depolarization, or amplitude damping. The results provide distinct analytical benchmarks for assessing noisy quantum resource generation.
main_problem: The study develops an analytical framework to quantify how initial quantum coherence is converted into entanglement within high-dimensional quantum systems (qunits) and analyzes the subsequent degradation of this entanglement under various noise channels.
main_result: The ideal conversion establishes a dimension-independent identity between input $\ell_1$-norm of coherence and output negativity. Different noise types degrade entanglement in distinct ways: phase damping causes uniform decay, depolarizing noise introduces pairwise sudden death thresholds, and amplitude damping shows asymmetric relaxation.
method: The analysis relies on calculating the negativity (a measure derived from the partial transpose) of the resulting bipartite state after applying controlled-shift operations followed by specific quantum noise channels.
model_or_system: The system involves two qudits ($A \otimes B$, dimension $n$), where one qudit acts as a coherent input and the other is an incoherent ancilla. The process models coherence-to-entanglement conversion via a generalized controlled-shift operation.
key_observables: Negativity ($N$), $\ell_1$-norm of coherence ($C_{\ell_1}$), entanglement sudden death thresholds, and decay factors for the negativity under noise.
important_parameters: System dimension ($n$), noise strength parameters (e.g., $p$ for damping), and the coefficients defining the input coherent state $|\psi_Aangle$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the three canonical noise channels—phase damping, global depolarizing noise, and amplitude damping—are applied sequentially after the initial controlled-shift operation.
figures_summary: Not specified in detail, but the notes imply tables summarizing general expressions for negativity under different noise models (e.g., Table I).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the ideal conversion identity ($N_0 \propto C_{\ell_1}$). It then systematically analyzes the effect of three distinct noise channels—phase damping, global depolarization, and amplitude damping—on this generated entanglement, deriving specific decay laws for each.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous analytical benchmarks for understanding resource conversion (coherence to entanglement) in high-dimensional quantum systems, which is crucial for designing robust quantum communication protocols that operate under realistic noise conditions.
